title: HDFC Bank Q2: Green Shoots Signal Future Growth
description: HDFC Bank reported a 4.7% year-on-year rise in net profit to ₹19,510 crore for Q2 FY27. Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined to a 12-quarter low of 3.16%, partl.

faq.q: What is Net Interest Margin (NIM) and why is it important for a bank?
faq.a: Net Interest Margin (NIM) is a key measure of a bank's profitability, representing the difference between the interest income a bank earns on its loans and the interest it pays on its deposits, relative to its total interest-earning assets. A higher NIM generally indicates better profitability.

faq.q: Why did HDFC Bank's NIM fall in Q2 FY27?
faq.a: HDFC Bank's NIM declined to a 12-quarter low, partly due to the interest outgo on Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) or FCNR (B) deposits raised in the previous quarter. The yield on assets also saw a decline.

faq.q: What does "asset quality improvement" mean for a bank?
faq.a: Asset quality improvement means that a bank has a lower proportion of bad loans (Non-Performing Assets or NPAs) in its loan book. For HDFC Bank, its Gross NPA decreased to 1.11% and Net NPA to 0.37%, indicating a healthier loan portfolio.

faq.q: How does HDFC Bank's performance compare to its peers?
faq.a: While HDFC Bank reported a 4.7% year-on-year net profit growth, some peers like ICICI Bank showed higher growth rates (e.g., 20.1% net profit increase) in Q2 FY27. This indicates a competitive environment within the private banking sector.

faq.q: What are "green shoots" in the context of bank results?
faq.a: "Green shoots" refer to early, positive signs that suggest a recovery or improvement in performance, even if the overall results still show some challenges. For HDFC Bank, these include core operating profit growth, improved asset quality, and a strategic shift towards higher-yielding loans to boost future margins.

faq.q: Does a dip in NIM directly affect my savings account interest rate?
faq.a: Not directly or immediately. While NIM reflects the bank's overall lending and deposit cost efficiency, individual savings account rates are influenced by broader market interest rates, RBI policies, and the bank's specific liquidity needs.

faq.q: What is the significance of FCNR (B) deposits?
faq.a: FCNR (B) deposits are foreign currency deposits accepted by Indian banks from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). They offer attractive interest rates and are a source of foreign currency funding for banks. Their interest outgo can sometimes impact NIM, as seen in HDFC Bank's Q2 results.
